items.title: Existing scene nodes are deleted by name without checking ownership

findings.title: Existing scene nodes are deleted by name without checking ownership
findings.evidence:
# Detects if a transfo node with the same name is already present
    prevTransfoNode = slicer.mrmlScene.GetFirstNodeByName('phantCalibTransfo')
    # if so, remove it
    if prevTransfoNode:
      slicer.mrmlScene.RemoveNode(prevTransfoNode)
    # Create the transfo node
findings.explanation: Opening the module initializes Phantom and removes the first existing node named phantCalibTransfo, even if it belongs to the user's current scene. Unsaved transform data can be lost. Similar name-based deletion occurs for model and connector nodes.
findings.suggestion: Keep references to nodes created by this module and remove only those it owns; let Slicer assign unique names when existing nodes conflict.

claude.reason: Phantom.py:29-34 removes the first node named 'phantCalibTransfo' and Phantom.py:61-63 removes 'PhantomModel'. Pointer.py:79, WorkingVolume.py:120,180 and AstmPhantomTest.py:262-264 do the same for other nodes. The names are specific to this module, so it is unlikely to hit unrelated user data. It would only remove a stale node from an earlier run of this module, or a user node that happens to share the name. This is an ordinary robustness issue, not a concrete path to harm, so not blocking.

gpt.reason: AstmPhantomTest/AstmPhantomTest.py:124-137,152 and 914-918 show that choosing the output folder initializes Phantom; AstmPhantomTest/AstmPhantomTestClasses/Phantom.py:28-34 says exactly: "    prevTransfoNode = slicer.mrmlScene.GetFirstNodeByName('phantCalibTransfo')" and "      slicer.mrmlScene.RemoveNode(prevTransfoNode)". No ownership check is made. A same-named unsaved node in the user's scene can be removed; this is a concrete data-loss path. items.title: Acquisition checks pointer status but not phantom-relative transform status

findings.title: Acquisition checks pointer status but not phantom-relative transform status
findings.explanation: After the initial connection check, a pointer-to-phantom update is accepted based only on PointerToTracker status. If the phantom is missing while the pointer remains tracked, an invalid or stale relative transform can enter the acquisition queue and affect measured points; the red status display does not itself halt acquisition. This is non-blocking correctness feedback.
findings.suggestion: Require valid status for the phantom and relative transforms as well, and abort or pause an active acquisition on tracking loss.

claude.reason: Pointer.py:205 checks self.ptrTransfoNode's TransformStatus inside onPtrRefTransformModified. It does not check ptrRefTransfoNode, which is the transform actually read on line 207. The status of the phantom-relative transform is therefore not validated there. I did not trace the handling of a missing phantom elsewhere, so the actual impact on acquisition is unconfirmed. It is a correctness weakness, not a safety issue.

gpt.reason: Pointer.py:203-212 says "    if self.ptrTransfoNode.GetAttribute(\"TransformStatus\") == \"OK\":" and "      self.pq.push(self.pos())"; lines 237-256 then accumulate and emit samples without checking relative or phantom status. AstmPhantomTest.py:771-794 checks all three only for initial startup, subsequently showing status through the border. If relative-transform events continue while the phantom is missing, stale or invalid data can affect an accuracy measurement; exact behavior depends on the tracker stream. This is non-blocking correctness feedback.

gemini.reason: Checked AstmPhantomTest/AstmPhantomTestClasses/Pointer.py:203-207 and AstmPhantomTest/AstmPhantomTest.py:734-794. In onPtrRefTransformModified, it checks `if self.ptrTransfoNode.GetAttribute("TransformStatus") == "OK":` instead of checking `self.ptrRefTransfoNode.GetAttribute("TransformStatus") == "OK"` (or both). If PointerToPhantom is MISSING while PointerToTracker is OK, stale/invalid relative transforms can be processed.

items.title: Session log captures unrelated Slicer logs and remains attached

findings.title: Modal directory dialog and global UI/logger side effects in widget `setup()`
findings.evidence:
self.saveDialog = qt.QFileDialog()
    self.saveDialog.setFileMode(qt.QFileDialog().DirectoryOnly)

    if self.saveDialog.exec():
      # Path where the ouput files (including the log) will be saved
      savePath = self.saveDialog.selectedFiles()[0]
      # The log file doesn't overwrite itself and is named after the date,
      # so any use of this module on a same day will be logged in the same file
      fh = logging.FileHandler(savePath + "/AstmPhantomTest_log_" + datetime.now().strftime("%Y.%m.%d") + ".log")
      fh.setLevel(logging.INFO)
      logging.getLogger().addHandler(fh)
findings.explanation: When the module widget is initialized (`setup`), it immediately blocks on a modal `QFileDialog.exec()`, resizes and maximizes the Slicer main window (lines 73-75), attaches a `FileHandler` to the root Python logger (`logging.getLogger().addHandler(fh)`) without removing it on cleanup, and starts an OpenIGTLink client connector on the default localhost port (`self.cnode.Start()`). Furthermore, if the user cancels the file dialog (`self.saveDialog.exec()` returns 0), `self.logic`, UI signal connections, and the OpenIGTLink connector are never initialized, leaving the module UI in a broken/unresponsive state for the rest of the Slicer session.
findings.suggestion: Avoid blocking modal dialogs, root logger mutations, and main window resizing inside `setup()`. Provide a directory selector widget (e.g., `ctkDirectoryButton`) in the module UI to choose the output folder and start the session explicitly.

items.title: Similarity calibration scales the reference distances used in accuracy results

findings.title: Similarity calibration scales the reference distances used in accuracy results
findings.evidence:
ldmkTransfo = vtk.vtkLandmarkTransform()
    ldmkTransfo.SetSourceLandmarks(ptsFrom)
    ldmkTransfo.SetTargetLandmarks(ptsTo)
    ldmkTransfo.SetModeToSimilarity()
    ldmkTransfo.Update()
    transfoMat = ldmkTransfo.GetMatrix()
    self.calibTransfoNode.SetMatrixTransformToParent(transfoMat)
findings.explanation: Similarity registration permits scale as well as rigid alignment. The resulting transform is applied to all CMM ground-truth points, and the scaled points are subsequently used for multi-point distance comparisons; a tracker scale error can therefore be partly absorbed into the reference and underreported. This is non-blocking correctness feedback.
findings.suggestion: Use rigid registration for the physical phantom reference, or justify and validate scaling separately and compare distances against the original CMM geometry.

claude.reason: Phantom.py:196 uses SetModeToSimilarity(), which allows scaling. Lines 201-205 apply the fitted transform to all ground-truth points. Scale error in the tracker can therefore be partly absorbed into the reference. This may be a deliberate design choice, and I could not verify the ASTM method's intent. It is a methodological point, not a defect that blocks anything.

gpt.reason: Phantom.py:190-205 fits CMM points to acquired points with "    ldmkTransfo.SetModeToSimilarity()" and then "      self.calGtPts[k] = np.array([p1[0], p1[1], p1[2]])". AstmPhantomTest.py:1249-1265 passes these points to the distance measurement, which computes "      gtDist = Dist(self.gtPts[kp[0]], self.gtPts[kp[1]])" and "      errors.append(abs(gtDist - ptrDist))" (Measurements.py:218-224). A fitted scale can therefore absorb a tracker scale error and reduce reported distance errors. This is non-blocking correctness feedback.

gemini.reason: Checked AstmPhantomTest/AstmPhantomTestClasses/Phantom.py:185-206, AstmPhantomTest/AstmPhantomTest.py:1250-1279, and AstmPhantomTest/AstmPhantomTestClasses/Measurements.py:218-225. `Phantom.calibrate()` uses `ldmkTransfo.SetModeToSimilarity()` (allowing isotropic scaling) and transforms `self.gtPts` into `self.calGtPts`. `self.calGtPts` is then passed to `distMeasurement.fullReset` / `setGtPts` and used in `updateDistStats` to compute ground-truth pairwise distances `gtDist = Dist(self.gtPts[kp[0]], self.gtPts[kp[1]])`, scaling the ground-truth reference distances instead of using rigid registration or unscaled CMM coordinates `Phantom.gtPts`.

items.title: Typo `msgBoxsgBox` raises NameError when point acquisition collects no samples

findings.title: Typo `msgBoxsgBox` raises NameError when point acquisition collects no samples
findings.evidence:
if np.size(self.coordAccumulator,0) == 0:
            msgBox = qt.QMessageBox()
            msgBox.setText("No sample taken during timer duration for point acquisition. Restart module and try again with increased duration.")
            msgBoxsgBox.setIcon(qt.QMessageBox().Warning)
            msgBoxsgBox.setStandardButtons(qt.QMessageBox().Ok)
            msgBoxsgBox.exec()
findings.explanation: In `Pointer.staticTimerCallback`, when no samples were collected during the point-acquisition timer duration, the code instantiates `msgBox` but then references `msgBoxsgBox` on the next three lines, raising a `NameError` instead of displaying the warning dialog to the user.

findings.title: No-sample acquisition error path references an undefined variable
findings.evidence:
if np.size(self.coordAccumulator,0) == 0:
          msgBox = qt.QMessageBox()
          msgBox.setText("No sample taken during timer duration for point acquisition. Restart module and try again with increased duration.")
          msgBoxsgBox.setIcon(qt.QMessageBox().Warning)

findings.explanation: If a timed acquisition receives no samples, the misspelled variable raises NameError instead of displaying the recovery instructions. This is non-blocking correctness feedback.
findings.suggestion: Use msgBox consistently and reset the acquisition state so the operator can retry.

findings.evidence:
set(RESOURCES_FILES
  Resources/gt/phantom.txt
  Resources/models/ftk250_RAS.stl
  Resources/models/ftk500_RAS.stl
  Resources/models/phantom2018_RAS.stl
  Resources/models/phantom2022_RAS.stl
findings.explanation: The repository commits two large binary STL meshes (`phantom2018_RAS.stl` at 10 MB and `phantom2022_RAS.stl` at 13 MB) and three large animated GIFs in `readme_img/` (6-8 MB each), and `AstmPhantomTest/CMakeLists.txt` omits `Resources/wv/PolarisVegaExt_ftk500Locs.txt` from `RESOURCES_FILES` so that working-volume preset is not installed in packaged builds.
findings.suggestion: Add `Resources/wv/PolarisVegaExt_ftk500Locs.txt` to `RESOURCES_FILES` in `AstmPhantomTest/CMakeLists.txt` if it is intended to be selectable in packaged builds, and consider simplifying or decimating the visual phantom STL meshes.
